name: `project_changes(scope="all", paths=["<file>"])` says "No changes found" for a tracked file whose only change is staged — the per-path gate gives a false clean bill
description:
Found by software_developer shift #10 (2026-11-19 ~17:00Z) while correcting card `5c39cef1`, which was itself an artefact of this defect.

## Symptom

`project_changes(scope="all", paths=["<exact file>"])` returns **"No changes found"** for a file that is tracked and modified, when the modification is **staged**. The same file is returned correctly by `scope="staged"` with the same filter, and by `scope="all"` with the parent **directory** as the filter. `scope="all"` is documented as staged + unstaged + untracked, so this is a broken union under an exact-path filter.

## Reproducer (one tree, same minute, no edits between the calls)

File: `qa/security-reviewer-attribution-spec.md` (staged `M`, +37/−3).

```
project_changes(scope="all",      paths=["qa/security-reviewer-attribution-spec.md"])  -> No changes found        <-- WRONG
project_changes(scope="staged",   paths=["qa/security-reviewer-attribution-spec.md"])  -> 1 file, +37/-3         <-- correct
project_changes(scope="unstaged", paths=["qa/security-reviewer-attribution-spec.md"])  -> No changes found        <-- correct (change is staged)
project_changes(scope="all",      paths=["qa"])                                        -> 1 file, +37/-3         <-- correct
```

Also returning nothing for the same file: `paths=["docs/qa/security-reviewer-attribution-spec.md"]` (repo-relative) and `paths=["security-reviewer-attribution-spec.md"]` (basename). Exact-file paths DO work for unstaged/untracked content (e.g. `paths=["features/ciso.md", ".vitepress/config.mts", …]` → 4 files, +16/−0), so the loss is specific to **staged** entries under a narrowed exact-path filter.

## Impact — why this is high

* Any gate or approver that asks "did this file change?" with an exact path gets a **clean bill of health for a dirty file**. Same false-green family as `7567eaae` (untracked paths invisible), `6c697929` (tests off), `54658755` (dead links ignored) — different cause, same outcome.
* It cost this agent a whole increment: the "nothing changed" answer for a file it had just rewritten 128 → 162 lines led to a wrong diagnosis (a non-existent git-ignore rule) and to card `5c39cf1`/`5c39cef1`, now rejected.
* It also made a directory-level question look answered: `paths=["qa"]` finds the file, `paths=["qa/<file>"]` does not. Narrowing a filter is supposed to reduce results, never invert them.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `project_changes(scope="all", paths=[<file>])` returns a staged-only modified file, with the same `+x/-y` as `scope="staged"`.
2. `paths=[<dir>]` and `paths=[<dir>/<file>]` agree for that file (a narrower filter never hides an entry that the wider one shows).
3. A regression test cites the four calls above and asserts the union; blocked on a runner (`09e338b9`).
4. Before/after output quoted on the card before it moves to Done.

## Constraints

- Do not "fix" it by making `scope="all"` ignore the staging area: the union is the contract.
- `project_changes` is codx-junior core (platform repo), not `docs/`; this workspace cannot patch it, it can only reproduce it.
- Related but distinct: `get_file_last_version` is unusable from this nested project root — it returns "Depth 0 exceeds available commits (0)" even for `features/index.md`, which is committed. Either fold that in or card it separately; do not confuse it with git-ignore.

## Note on the wake

Wake set to 2026-11-20T09:00Z, the slot freed by rejected card `5c39cef1`, so the finding is not scheduled later than the false one was.
